How are you ACTUALLY supposed to use "try-except" clauses?

When you develop software you have 3 situations.

  • It succeeds
  • It fails, but can recover and retry
  • It fails miserably (and can only abort)

A lot of developers abuse the try-except because they are lazy and don't want tor return a false. This works with small code but when you abuse it like that then your except clause will become more and more complex to a point where you have no more control.

The exception handling should only be used for extreme and rare conditions where the code has no clue what to do with it. If it is a normal fail then he should return a correct fail return value and never trigger an exception. It is a bit more work but in the end when your code scales massively it stays easier to maintain and handle.

Throwing exceptions should be rare. Not the norm.
Don't spam them, use them for things related to "well, this program really shouldn't be running if this isn't true, so exception and (return 0 or exit or whatever it is that closes your program).
